title: Eddie Howe has ‘no doubt’ he is right head coach for Newcastle
content:
Eddie Howe has “no doubt” that he is still the man to lead Newcastle United forwards and is adamant he would “step aside and let someone else do it” if that perception changed within his own mind.

The Newcastle head coach is facing the most difficult spell of his four-and-a-half-year tenure at St James’ Park, with his side 12th in the Premier League and having ceded the Carabao Cup midweek.

Following Saturday’s poor 3-2 home defeat to Brentford, Howe admitted he needed to look at himself and “work better”. Less than 48 hours on, at his press conference ahead of what Howe described as a “massive game” against Tottenham Hotspur in the league on Tuesday, the head coach reaffirmed his desire to fight on.

“No, there’s no doubt in my mind and that’s why I’m sat here,” Howe said, when asked if he had any doubt in his mind as to whether he was the right man for the job. “If there was (doubt), then I wouldn’t be because the club’s the most important thing.

“I’d never put myself before the club if I didn’t think I was the correct man to take the team forward and I could give the players what they need, then I would step aside and let someone else do it.

“The club’s always number one, and from my perspective I’ve got to think that I am the right person for the job, and I’m giving value and I’m helping the players, and I’m the right person to get results, ultimately.

“So as long as I feel that in my heart and in my spirit, then my desire and my motivation levels are as high as they’ve ever been. But I think that’s the key question I always have to ask myself: ‘Am I the right person to take the team and the club forward?’.”

Internally, Newcastle’s hierarchy are firmly supportive of Howe, even if they accept results and performances are below what is expected.

Yet disquiet is building among sections of the fanbase, though Howe insists outside noise cannot heap greater pressure on him, given how committed he is to his role.

“I care so much about what I do, I care so much about the club,” Howe said. “The club for me is always number one. Not myself, not any of the players to a degree, it’s the club and what that stands for.

“Of course the players are a huge part of that. So I will always act in the best interest of the club with every decision that I make, whether that’s about me or about any individual player.

“So I think when you’re trying to act in that way and you’re trying to think of the bigger picture, the pressure that individuals or other people can put on you, it’s irrelevant really. I have to live with my own thoughts of myself and what I’m delivering.”
